title: Remembering rare floods
bodyMd:
Residents of a river town often described the previous decade as unusually safe because no flood had entered the main square. An engineer cautioned that the square had recently been raised, while nearby low-lying streets continued to flood. The town's most visible landmark had ceased to be a stable indicator of the river's behaviour. A change in what residents could see had become a change in what they remembered as the town's flood history.

This did not mean local memories were simply false. People accurately recalled the square remaining dry. The difficulty arose when a true observation about one altered place was generalised to the whole town. The engineer combined oral accounts with elevation records and photographs from several streets, treating memories as located observations rather than interchangeable measurements of a single event.
